messages.subject: Outlier traps
parts:
Hello! I am using SECR to estimate badger density. Cages were used to trap and mark animals followed by a grid of cameras for resighting. Two of the traps are quite a distance from the other traps and cameras. See the image attached (sorry, maps not very sophisticated yet!); the two traps in the SW corner are about 1.6km from the nearest camera. 
 
Animals marked at these traps were resighted on cameras in the grid, however I'm not sure if this is a weird sampling design that might affect the model, since the area in between the cameras and these traps was not sampled. Do you have any advice about whether I should exclude these individuals from analysis?

Many thanks!

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Outlier traps
parts:
Hello
Sorry I missed your post when it came in. I assume you are using spatial mark-resight models. Yes, it's a weird 'sampling design' if it can be called that. No, it won't in itself be a problem for the model, which is (almost) infinitely adaptable, given assumptions of uniform density and behaviour. However, the fact you got resightings at 1.6 km suggests the scale of sampling was otherwise inadequate - estimates of the scale of detection will rest almost entirely on a couple of detections of a couple of animals, and be sensitive to the choice of detection function. Unfortunately, you're stuck now that you know there can be large-scale movements. Clipping to the scale of the other detectors will deliver answers, but they will be wrong. Maybe I'm being too dogmatic (other opinions welcome), but that's where it seems to lead.
Murray
